gloss: chitose-ame; long candy given at Shichi-Go-San

definitions.gloss: chitose-ame; long red-and-white stick candy for Shichi-Go-San
definitions.explanation: A long, thin, red-and-white stick candy given to children at {七五三|しちごさん} (Shichi-Go-San). Its length symbolizes a wish for the child's long life and healthy growth. The name literally means "thousand-year candy."

examples.japanese: {千歳飴|ちとせあめ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦もらった→もらう：00520_morau⟧。
{子|こ}ども⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{千歳飴|ちとせあめ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{袋|ふくろ}→袋：00837_fukuro⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{持|も}って→持つ：00478_motsu⟧⟦{笑|わら}っている→笑う：00685_warau⟧。
examples.english: The child is smiling, holding a bag of chitose-ame.

examples.japanese: ⟦{七五三|しちごさん}→七五三：06185_shichigosan⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、⟦{長寿|ちょうじゅ}→長寿：14478_chouju⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{願|ねが}って→願う：02387_negau⟧{子|こ}ども⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{千歳飴|ちとせあめ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{贈|おく}る→贈る：09862_okuru⟧。
examples.english: At Shichi-Go-San, chitose-ame is given to children to wish them a long life.

notes:
Written {千|ち} (thousand) + {歳|とせ} (years) + ⟦{飴|あめ}→飴：00687_ame⟧ (candy). The candy comes in a decorated bag printed with auspicious motifs such as cranes, turtles, and pine.

CULTURAL NOTE:
- Sold at shrines and confectioners around ⟦{七五三|しちごさん}→七五三：06185_shichigosan⟧ (November 15th)
- The thin, very long shape represents a wish for long, healthy life
- Often shared with relatives and neighbors after the shrine visit
